text:
### Observed differences

- The relative order of two activity groups reversed. In the earlier window, A20, A21, A22, A24 and A25 consistently ran before A29, before A33 and before the group A19/A23/A26/A27/A28 — for example, A20 preceded A29 in about 99 in 100 traces and A33 in about 98 in 100. In the later window, every one of the 30 measured cross-pairs flipped direction: A29 preceded A20 in about 98 in 100 traces, A33 preceded A20 in about 98 in 100, and pairs within the optional activities reversed as well (A24 ran before A23 in about 20 in 100 traces before and never after; A23 before A24 rose from 0 to about 19 in 100). [REL001, REL004, REL005, REL014, REL016, REL021, REL025, REL027, REL029]

- The two groups also exchanged their halves of the trace (event positions, not clock time). A20–A25 moved from a mean relative position of about 0.39–0.40 to about 0.64, while A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 moved from about 0.69 to about 0.32–0.36; A29 (about 0.49 to 0.37) and A33 (about 0.67 to 0.55) shifted earlier but stayed between the groups. Participation was essentially unchanged: A20–A25, A29 and A33 still occur in all traces, and A19/A23/A26/A27/A28 each in about 17–27 in 100 traces in both windows. [POS001, POS002, POS005, POS008, POS009, POS010, POS011, POS012]

- Successors swapped sides. Before, the observed outgoing transitions of A19, A23, A26, A27 and A28 went almost exclusively to A34 (about 90–100 in 100); in the later window they go to A29 (about 92–100 in 100). Before, A20–A25 each sent about 15–29 in 100 of their outgoing transitions to A29; in the later window that share goes to A34 instead (about 18–22 in 100). A33's successors changed from the A19/A23/A26–A28 group to the A20–A25 group, and A44's from the A20–A25 group to the A19/A23/A26–A28 group. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR005, DIR007, DIR008, DIR010, DIR011, DIR012]

- Close successions changed sides. Before, A33 was followed by A34 within about two steps in about 97 in 100 traces, and A27 and A28 were followed by A34 within one step in nearly all their traces; in the later window each of these pairs is within five steps in only about 1 trace in 200. Conversely, A20→A34, A21→A34 and A33→A20/A21/A25, previously seen in about 1 trace each, now occur in about 190–199 traces, and A26 and A26-after-A44 are now immediately followed by A29 and A26 respectively. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG005, LAG006, LAG009, LAG010, LAG011, LAG012]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, two blocks of activities have exchanged their order: the block A20, A21, A22, A24, A25, which previously ran before A29 and A33 and before the block A19, A23, A26, A27, A28, now runs after them, with A29 and A33 still lying between the two blocks; A34, previously reached from the A19/A23/A26–A28 block, is now reached from the A20–A25 block, and A44 now leads into the A19/A23/A26–A28 block instead of the A20–A25 block. [REL004, REL021, DIR002, DIR005, DIR011, DIR012, LAG010]

The reversal is shown directly by the relational items, which cover all 30 cross-pairs between the two blocks and the fixed activities A29 and A33 with co-occurrence levels unchanged; the positional shifts move the two blocks in opposite directions by similar amounts; the successor and adjacency changes mirror the same swap; and participation shares are stable, so this is a reordering rather than activities being added, removed or repeated differently. The 66 qualifying control-flow items are many times the fewer than 1 expected by chance among the 176 tested units, so sampling variation cannot explain the pattern as a whole. [REL001, REL016, POS002, POS005, DIR005, LAG001, LAG010]

Limitations: several lag profiles rest on a single observation in one window, so only the appearance or disappearance of those close successions, not their exact distances, is well supported. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot fully exclude is a flip in the dominance of two pre-existing process variants rather than a re-routing within one variant, although the reversed order appeared in at most about 2 in 100 traces before and the original order in at most about 2 in 100 after, so such variants would have had to be very rare in one window each. [LAG001, LAG004, REL004, REL021]

Other differences: both windows show a fringe of low-share successors (about 0.5–3 in 100 of outgoing transitions, e.g. A20→A45, A22→A01/A07, A33→A17/A35, A44→A04) whose targets differ between the windows; these are too small to support a separate behavioural hypothesis. [DIR002, DIR004, DIR011, DIR012]
